 Game 12 Hub: New York Rangers vs. Ottawa Senators
 Ary M 
 Oct 24, 2026 
 3 min 
 No Ullmark vs. Shesterkin, but Stützle vs. Lafrenière is still a tantalizing matchup on Saturday night. 
 Photo by Mohamed / Unsplash 
 It's been an emotional week in Canada's capital: a valiant win against the Florida Panthers, followed by a let-down the next day against the San Jose Sharks.
 Tonight's game presents an opportunity to end this home stand on a high before the team embarks on a five-game road trip through California and Buffalo. 
 Here's what's on tap: 
 Sens lines
 Here's how Travis Green's group lined up this morning, with the only change being Burakovsky back in on a fourth-line rotation alongside Stephen Halliday and Nick Cousins. It's nice to see Captain Chabot back on the ice in a yellow non-contact jersey, and hopefully he's available to go on the team's road trip next week. 
 Ullmark, Eklund, and MacDermid remain out.

— Alex Adams (@alexadamssn.bsky.social) 2026-10-24T14:32:16.189Z Rangers lines
 Here's how Mike Sullivan's New York Rangers lined up most recently during their 5-4 loss to Toronto on Thursday. I expect Luke Glendening to play as the team's fourth-line centre since Justin Dowling was sent back down to AHL Hartford after the game, and defender Matthew Robertson is also an option after being called up. 
 The Rangers are missing both of their regular goaltenders, Shesterkin and Korpisalo, to long-term injuries, so the Sens will face either 24-year-old Dylan Garand or 31-year-old journeyman Spencer Martin in goal. Skaters Adam Sýkora, Aidan Thompson, and Joseph Veleno are also missing due to injury. 
 The lines at practice today look similar:
Perreault-Zibanejad-Lafreniere
Kartye-Miller-Dorofeyev
Cuylle-Laba-Tolvanen
Bjorkstrand-Dowling-Raddysh
(Glendening and Rempe rotated in)
Gavrikov-Fox
Pettersson-Morrow (in for Durzi)
Smits-Schneider
— ColinSNewsday (@colinsnewsday.bsky.social) 2026-10-21T15:18:52.950Z Game notes
 The Rangers are pretty top-heavy on forward and defence. If the Sens can get the matchups they want on Zibanejad and Miller, the other two lines should have an opportunity to tilt the ice. Gavrikov and Fox are Sullivan's do-it-all pairing, and I imagine he'll want them out against Stützle, so it might be worth giving Timmy a tough matchup to survive in order to open up space for the rest of his team. 
 Alexis Lafrenière took a while, but looks rejuvenated since Artemi Panarin's departure to the Los Angeles Kings. He leads New York in most meaningful categories, with one more goal but one less point than Stützle this season. 
 Alberts Smits, the Rangers' fifth overall pick last year, is sticking with the big club. He's been surviving his minutes with the rugged Braeden Schneider alongside him on defence, and is worth watching to compare his play to our rookie in Yakemchuk.
